profile.reading:
Avalon 3 is a Retelit data centre on Via Bisceglie in Milan, the third and largest building of the Avalon Campus, which Retelit markets as a single virtual campus formed by Avalon 1, Avalon 2 and Avalon 3 linked together.

Retelit publishes a fairly full specification for this building. It gives 3,500 square metres of floor area, ground floor loading rated at 1,500 kilograms per square metre, and 3.2 MW of IT power. That last figure is stated by the operator specifically as IT power, so it is recorded here as IT load rather than as a utility service size, and Retelit does not publish the utility supply, the transformer capacity, or the ratings of the redundant generators and UPS systems it says the building has. Cooling is described as sustainable and redundant, running at a power usage effectiveness of 1.3, on electricity Retelit describes as 100 percent renewable. The building carries ANSI/TIA-942 Rating 4 certification both as designed and as built, ISO 22237 certification, Uptime Institute Tier IV certification, and LEED v4 Gold for environmental sustainability. Interconnection runs through what Retelit calls a distributed meet-me room reaching across the campus, giving access to more than 170 carriers, over the top providers, cloud platforms and content delivery networks. The site is guarded around the clock, with video surveillance using motion detection, and monitored from a network operations centre.

The most distinctive published feature of the building is heat reuse. Reporting on the project describes waste heat from Avalon 3 feeding Milan's district heating network, operated by the utility A2A, from 2026, supplying an estimated 2.5 MW of thermal output and enough heat for roughly 1,250 homes. That thermal figure is heat recovered from the building and is a different quantity from the 3.2 MW of IT load, and the two should not be added or compared.

The map record behind this row has a longer history than the building. The OpenStreetMap way was first drawn in November 2010 as a plain building, changed to building=office in May 2019, and only in November 2022 did a mapper add the name Avalon 3, the operator Irideos, a website and a start_date of 11 November 2022. In September 2025 another mapper updated the operator to Retelit, added the telecom=data_center tag and pointed the website at the Avalon Campus site. The 11 November 2022 date is a mapper supplied tag rather than an operator published commissioning date, and Retelit's own facility page gives no opening date, so this registry treats that date as unconfirmed.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-05. Two changes of substance. First, the prior source list included it.wikipedia.org, a banned source for this registry, and the Retelit corporate history drawn from it (1996 e-Planet origin, 2000 listing, 43,000 km of fibre, AAE-1 consortium, 2021 delisting, Asterion tender offer, a 100 million euro AI investment) could not be re-verified this pass from a permitted primary source, so it was removed rather than left standing on a banned citation. Second, added OSM provenance from the object history: way 86005985 v1 2010-11-21 matbech building=yes, v2 2019-05-17 Alecs01 building=office, v3 2022-11-12 mascalzone67 added name/operator=Irideos/start_date=2022-11-11, v5 2025-09-08 c674a changed operator to Retelit and added telecom=data_center. start_date is therefore mapper supplied and is flagged as unconfirmed in the text. Power discipline: 3.2 MW is published by the operator as IT power, the 2.5 MW district heating figure is thermal output and is kept separate. WebSearch quota exhausted this session.
